findings.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — [P2, confidence 100] `if website_host == discourse_host` compares DNS hostnames without canonicalization, so a profile URL `http://EXAMPLE.COM/user` on the `example.com` instance is treated as external and drops `/user`, violating the same-domain path display contract.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144 — [P2, confidence 75] `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` encodes a one-label subdomain model, so `www.example.com/user` on an instance at `community.forum.example.com` is the same registered domain but returns only `www.example.com`, dropping the path; the author's simplest rebuttal is that only one subdomain level is supported, but the serializer's stated parent-domain rule has no such invariant and the ad-hoc shape makes the next hostname topology change silently misrender URLs.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — [P1, confidence 100] `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` displays a full path for distinct sibling hosts such as `www.example.com` and `forum.example.com`, violating the requirement that paths appear only when the website domain is the instance domain.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — P2, confidence 100, `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` displays a complete path for sibling subdomains such as `www.example.com` on `forum.example.com`, changing the stated same-instance-domain-only UX without explicit acceptance.

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:94 — P3 confidence 75: `Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('forums.example.com')` expands the requested exact-instance-domain UX into parent-domain matching, so a profile pointing to example.com on forums.example.com exposes its full path despite the task requiring it only when the website domain is the same as the instance domain.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — [P1, confidence 100] `def include_website_name; website.present?; end` serializes `website_name` to anonymous viewers whenever a profile has a website, bypassing the adjacent `untrusted_attributes :website` restriction and disclosing a restricted user's website hostname and same-instance URL path.

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76 — [confidence 75][P2] The new tests assert only `expect(json[:website_name]).to eq 'example.com/user'` and never render `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so a client model/template wiring regression that hides the website label on every profile passes while the changed user-facing behavior is broken.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — [P2, confidence 100] `if website_host == discourse_host` compares DNS hostnames without canonicalization, so a profile URL `http://EXAMPLE.COM/user` on the `example.com` instance is treated as external and drops `/user`, violating the same-domain path display contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at line 141 compares `website_host == discourse_host` using direct string comparison without any case normalization. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive per RFC, so 'EXAMPLE.COM' and 'example.com' should be treated as the same domain. The code uses `URI(website.to_s).host` which preserves the original case from the URL, meaning a URL like 'http://EXAMPLE.COM/user' would have website_host='EXAMPLE.COM' which would not equal discourse_host='example.com', causing the path to be dropped when it should be included. This is a real edge case bug in the hostname comparison logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144 — [P2, confidence 75] `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` encodes a one-label subdomain model, so `www.example.com/user` on an instance at `community.forum.example.com` is the same registered domain but returns only `www.example.com`, dropping the path; the author's simplest rebuttal is that only one subdomain level is supported, but the serializer's stated parent-domain rule has no such invariant and the ad-hoc shape makes the next hostname topology change silently misrender URLs.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real edge case bug in the website_name logic. Looking at the diff, the condition on line 142-143 checks `discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` and compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` with `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`. For a website like `www.example.com/user` on an instance at `community.forum.example.com`, the lengths differ (3 vs 4), so this branch won't match. It falls through to the else branch which checks `discourse_host.ends_with?('.' << website_host)` - this would be checking if `community.forum.example.com` ends with `.www.example.com`, which is false, so it returns just `website_host` without the path. This is inconsistent with the stated goal of showing the full path when domains are related. The finding correctly identifies that the logic has edge cases where related domains don't get the path appended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — [P1, confidence 100] `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` displays a full path for distinct sibling hosts such as `www.example.com` and `forum.example.com`, violating the requirement that paths appear only when the website domain is the instance domain.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logic issue. Looking at the code on line 146, when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and both have more than 2 parts, and their parent domains match (e.g., www.example.com vs forum.example.com), the code returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. This means for sibling subdomains like www.example.com and forum.example.com, it would show the full path (e.g., 'www.example.com/user'). However, based on the test cases, paths should only be shown when the website domain IS the instance domain or is a parent of it, not for sibling subdomains. The test only covers cases where domains are the same or where website is parent of instance, not sibling subdomains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — P2, confidence 100, `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` displays a complete path for sibling subdomains such as `www.example.com` on `forum.example.com`, changing the stated same-instance-domain-only UX without explicit acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at line 146 shows the complete path (website_host + path) for sibling subdomains (e.g., www.example.com on forum.example.com). Looking at the diff, the condition checks if both hosts have the same number of parts (>2) and if their parent domains match, then it returns the full path. The tests only cover: different domains, same domain, and parent domain cases - but there's no test for the sibling subdomain case (www.example.com vs forum.example.com). This is a legitimate scope/design concern about whether this behavior is intentional, though it's not a bug per se - it's a design decision that may need explicit acceptance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:94 — P3 confidence 75: `Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('forums.example.com')` expands the requested exact-instance-domain UX into parent-domain matching, so a profile pointing to example.com on forums.example.com exposes its full path despite the task requiring it only when the website domain is the same as the instance domain.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the intent of the code. Looking at the diff, the `website_name` method in user_serializer.rb explicitly handles the case where the website domain is a parent of the instance domain (line: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host`). The test at line 94 correctly verifies this intentional behavior - when the instance is at 'forums.example.com' and the website is 'example.com/user', it should show the full path because example.com is the parent domain. This is a deliberate design decision, not a bug. The finding incorrectly claims this 'expands' beyond the task requirements, but the code and tests show this parent-domain matching is intentional functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — [P1, confidence 100] `def include_website_name; website.present?; end` serializes `website_name` to anonymous viewers whenever a profile has a website, bypassing the adjacent `untrusted_attributes :website` restriction and disclosing a restricted user's website hostname and same-instance URL path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security issue. Looking at the diff, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 43 shows it's part of the attributes list, and the file has `def self.untrusted_attributes(*attrs)` at line 40). The new `website_name` attribute is added to the regular attributes list (line 43) but NOT to untrusted_attributes. The `include_website_name` method only checks `website.present?` without any trust level verification. This means `website_name` will be serialized for all users regardless of trust level, while `website` itself is restricted. This is a security bypass that exposes website information (hostname and potentially path) to anonymous/untrusted viewers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76 — [confidence 75][P2] The new tests assert only `expect(json[:website_name]).to eq 'example.com/user'` and never render `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so a client model/template wiring regression that hides the website label on every profile passes while the changed user-facing behavior is broken.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new tests only verify the serializer's website_name output but don't test the template/model integration. The diff shows changes to both the serializer (adding website_name) and the template (changing from {{websiteName}} to {{model.website_name}}), but the tests only cover the serializer. However, this is a valid architectural concern about test coverage - if the model doesn't properly expose website_name from the serializer response, the template would fail silently. This is a legitimate missing integration test concern, not a bug in the code itself.
